basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 8.' and it opens 'Vers. 8. Et cum audissent vocem Domini Dei. Deus primo homini per subjectam creaturam, id'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 8. Et cum audissent vocem Domini Dei. Deus primo homini per subjectam creaturam, id est, per angelum sub humana specie apparentem loquebatur: unde et vocem Domini audisse dicitur. Nec vacat, quod post meridiem eamdem vocem percepisse dicitur, quando jam dies a calore suo frigescit: quia jam in eo fervor charitatis et lux veritatis defecerat. Unde nona hora spiritum emisit, qui sexta hora fuerat crucifixus. Et recte hoc ordine actum est, ut qua hora homo de paradiso ejectus est eadem illuc | restitueretur.
